lines.text: It sounds like a man protecting evidence, and it IS evidence - so here's the protocol. Don't touch that card again. Copy the file to two places - a computer and a fresh card - and put the original in an envelope. Never enhance it yourself: enhancement software invents pixels, and any analyst worth his salt discards an enhanced file on sight. What real eyes look at: the frame rate, the timestamp, how the object moves against the trees - parallax - and whether the light behaves like your own headlights bouncing back. Then the copies go to a photo analyst or a field investigator. Originals, not screenshots. Screenshots are how good footage dies.

lines.text: Your instinct evidences proper handling - the card is evidence. Protocol: cease handling the original; duplicate the file to two independent media; envelope the original. Prohibition: self-enhancement - interpolation artifacts invalidate files with trained analysts. Examination criteria: frame rate integrity, embedded timestamp, motion parallax against fixed background, and photometric consistency with headlight reflection. Submit duplicates to a photographic analyst or field investigator. Original files only - screenshots lack forensic value.

lines.text: Your brother did moth analysis on a screenshot - that's not a rebuttal, that's a guess with family privileges. Here's how to settle it yourself, no expert required: play the file frame by frame. A moth on the lens stays the same size and soft at the edges. A thing crossing your beams shrinks with distance and moves against the trees. Three seconds at thirty frames is ninety frames - count what happens to the size. If it shrinks, it wasn't a bug. If it doesn't, your brother owes you an apology. Either way, you'll know before anybody laughs.
